extracted.intended_audience: readers planning a short (36-hour) visit to Brooklyn — tourists and local visitors seeking a weekend itinerary
extracted.subtask_description: Create a compact 36-hour travel itinerary for Brooklyn that highlights neighborhoods, attractions, dining, nightlife, shopping, lodging, transit options, and suggested times; aims to be low-prep and walkable. The piece should balance cultural events, food recommendations, and practical details (prices, hours, transit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid most touristy/overdeveloped areas
rubrics_metrics.description: This itinerary skips the most touristy and overdeveloped areas, including Williamsburg and Dumbo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on neighborhoods that feel more local and less heavily touristed; explicitly call out which popular areas are being avoided (examples given: Williamsburg, Dumbo) so readers know the editorial stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No restaurant reservations or advance planning required
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires no restaurant reservations or advance planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize walk-in, casual, or easily accessed food and activities so the 36-hour plan is feasible on short notice; highlight places that accept walk-ins and note when reservations would be necessary if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight seasonal and free cultural events
rubrics_metrics.description: Include concerts in Prospect Park, a show-stopping exhibition at the Brooklyn Museum and other seasonal draws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out free or seasonal events (example: 'Celebrate Brooklyn!' at the Lena Horne Bandshell presented by BRIC) and provide current lineup or exhibition names and dates when possible so readers can plan around them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer geographically diverse dining recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend fantastic food far and wide, from tacos in Bushwick and dumplings in Sunset Park to nostalgic soft serves in southern Brooklyn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include neighborhood-specific food picks spanning different cuisines and price points; give examples of specialties (e.g., pan-fried pork-and-chive dumplings, Sicilian-style pizza squares) to help readers choose based on taste and location.

rubrics_metrics.name: List key stops with concise identifying details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a 'Key stops' section naming venues and what they are known for (shops, parks, museums, performance venues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each key stop, include a short phrase explaining its appeal (e.g., Radio Bakery — Earl Grey morning buns; Brooklyn Museum — current exhibition 'Giants') so readers can quickly scan for interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe attractions and why to visit them
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention attractions (parks, gardens, boardwalks, parkside views) and highlight notable features or experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what each attraction offers (views, recreational areas, art installations) and any unique character (e.g., Riegelmann Boardwalk attracts a colorful cast of characters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Give dining details including specialties and sample prices
rubrics_metrics.description: For dining entries, list specialties and include prices where available (e.g., sandwiches $14.50, ice cream from $6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing example menu items and prices helps readers budget and choose; note unusual ordering/house rules (e.g., cash-only spots like Kai Feng Fu Dumpling House).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend bars and nightlife with vibe and programming
rubrics_metrics.description: List bars and music venues with descriptions of atmosphere, typical programming, and any notable features (e.g., zebra-print carpeting at Danger Danger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the vibe (dive bar, jazz club, multi-room club), typical performers or nightly offerings, cover charges when relevant, and whether a spot is longstanding or newly opened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include shopping and market recommendations with specialties
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend markets, bookstores, boutiques and what makes them notable (e.g., Fort Greene Park Greenmarket, The Word is Change with social-justice focus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out the kinds of goods sold (artisan stalls, vintage Black-culture miscellany, records) so readers can target shopping stops that match interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accommodation options with distinguishing features and price ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to stay: list hotels with notable amenities and starting room rates (e.g., 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge — rooms start at $680; Ace Hotel Brooklyn — rooms start at $279).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include location cues, unique selling points (rooftop pool, pet-friendly, industrial-chic), and approximate prices to help readers choose lodging that fits budget and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain getting-around logistics and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting around: note walkability and list transit options with typical fares (subways and buses $2.90; ferries $4; Citi Bike rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete price figures and describe available modes (subway, bus, ferry, Citi Bike, ride-hailing) plus practical notes about bike docks or e-bikes and pass options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer a timed day-by-day itinerary with suggested sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An itinerary organized by day and time (Friday, Saturday, Sunday) with specific activities at scheduled times (e.g., 4 p.m. bike along the waterfront; 6 p.m. dine; 7:30 p.m. attend a free concert).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give start times, suggested durations and logical geographic sequencing to make the plan executable in 36 hours; include transit or walking suggestions between stops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply price and ticketing information for attractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include admission prices and ticket details when relevant (e.g., Brooklyn Museum tickets $25; Brooklyn Botanic Garden admission $22; last entry times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention seasonality, dates (exhibition through July 7), and last-entry times to help readers plan visiting order and avoid disappointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include practical/local context and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention local conditions and policy changes that affect visitors (humidity, bugs, city odors, gentrification, enforcement of strict new short-term rental rules in 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide candid context about neighborhood character and recent policy changes or construction projects so readers have realistic expectations and avoid surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide indoor alternatives or contingencies for weather/bugs
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest indoor options when outdoor plans are affected (e.g., when mosquitoes descend after dark, head indoors for an encore performance at LunÀtico or visit Public Records Upstairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer backup indoor venues and note typical triggers for switching plans (mosquitoes, bad weather) so the 36-hour plan remains flexible.
